rv.q: Miller brilliantly captures the profound ache of a family broken by its own web of lies and a world that values economic success over humanity.
All My Sons is an impactful piece, and the first must-see for devoted Boston theatergoers this season.
The unity of this production’s design elements matches the unity of its actors and creates a cohesive production worth making time to see.
Lyric Stage’s All My Sons is so jaw droppingly good, I would gladly see it again.
Arthur Miller's "ALL MY SONS" continues in Boston until October 18 th and is a fabulous way to kick off Lyric Stage Company's latest season.
All My Sons remains haunting because Miller’s central question has lost none of its force: Where does our responsibility end—with ourselves, with our families, or with people we may never know?
This “All My Sons” is a powder keg of a production whose fuse is lit early on and slowly burns while we watch and wait.
Scott Edmiston’s sharply acted Lyric Stage revival of Arthur Miller’s 1947 drama reveals the moral rot lurking beneath postwar suburban prosperity—and its unsettling relevance today.

cn.t: Lyric Stage's sharply acted revival proves Miller's 1947 drama remains powerfully relevant, with critics praising powerhouse performances and Scott Edmiston's well-paced direction of this compelling, indelible tragedy.
